title: Array Parameters
concept: When passing an array to a function, it is too large, so only the ‘first address’ is sent.

steps.title: with header
steps.explanation:
Use the output function with `#include <stdio.h>`.

This lesson covers the behavior of array decay to address when passing array arguments.

steps.title: printArr function definition
steps.explanation:
In `printArr(int arr[], int len)`, `arr[]` behaves like a pointer in a function parameter.

So, you can safely traverse only by receiving the length `len` separately.

steps.title: Start main function
steps.explanation: The main frame is created and prepares the array `data`.

steps.title: Array declaration and initialization
steps.explanation:
Store 10, 20, and 30 in contiguous memory in the `data` array.

The array name serves as a starting point for the address of the first element.

steps.title: Passing an Array (Array Decay)
steps.explanation:
When calling `printArr(data, 3);`, `data` is passed decayed to the starting address.

That is, the function accesses based on the original position rather than a copy of the array.

steps.title: for loop traversal
steps.explanation:
Print elements in order with `arr[i]`.

Internally, it has the same meaning as `*(arr+i)` pointer access.

steps.title: Program exit
steps.explanation:
Exit with `return 0;`.

Key point: In array argument passing, address and length must be managed together.

quiz.question: If you declare void func(int a[100]), how does the compiler interpret it?
quiz.explanation:
Numbers in square brackets are ignored.
An array declaration in place of a function parameter is unconditionally equivalent to a pointer declaration.

misconceptions.wrong: Arrays can be passed by Call by Value.
misconceptions.why: If you really want to do it, put an array in a struct and pass the struct to copy it (tip).

keyTakeaway: Array arguments are actually pointers. So the original has to be modified, and the length has to be taken care of separately.
